extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of Milton, Early Modern English, and literary annotation
extracted.subtask_description: Provide line-by-line scholarly notes and glosses on Milton's Areopagitica: explain obsolete words and usages, give etymologies and cognates, cite parallel passages (biblical, classical, and contemporaries), and supply historical/contextual information and textual commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Etymology and word history
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace the origin and historical development of a word (e.g. 'cAo/> = exchange' from A.-S. cedpan; 'piddling' probably connected with Fr. petit; 'feature' from Lat. factura).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give language-of-origin, related cognates (Dutch, German, Latin, Greek, French), variant historical forms (e.g. 'Malvesie', 'mabnesyne'), and note semantic shifts over time. Examples in the notes: derivations for 'cheap/chop', 'arrant', 'feature', 'publicans', 'starch/stark'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain obsolete or specialized meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and explain senses of words or phrases that are archaic or differ from modern usage (e.g. 'voided out of the Church' = emptied out of; 'step' in step-mother originally implying bereft).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the historical sense, contrast with modern sense, and give literary or legal examples where appropriate (Chaucer, Fabyan, Biblical, or legal usage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and syntactic construction notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out and explicate grammatical constructions specific to Early Modern/Elizabethan English (e.g. intransitive 'startle', factitive use 'remember them' = make them remember, pleonastic negatives 'who cannot but discern').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain construction, indicate modern equivalent or preferred form, and supply parallel citations (King Lear, Macbeth, Shakespeare sonnets). The notes highlight usage distinctions such as 'does' as complete verb vs. auxiliary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage and register (dialectal, colloquial, rhetorical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note registers, dialectal survivals, schoolboy or provincial usages, and rhetorical functions (e.g. 'Chop is still common... in provincial dialects, and amongst schoolboys').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate where usage is provincial, colloquial, or rhetorical; cite comparable contemporary occurrences (e.g. Lydgate, Chaucer, Pepys).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references to scripture, classical, and contemporary texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide parallel passages and authorities (biblical citations, classical authors, Milton's contemporaries) to illuminate imagery and phrasing (e.g. Matt. xvi.18; Psalm references; Plutarch, Ovid, Tacitus, Jeremy Taylor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise references (book, chapter, verse or work and line), explain relevance to the passage, and quote short parallels where helpful (numerous examples throughout the notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and cultural context
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply historical background or cultural information needed to understand references (e.g. Loretto as a medieval pilgrimage site; history of printing/newspapers in Turkey; St. Thomas and London commerce).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dates, brief narrative of relevant events or institutions, and bibliographic pointers (Murray, Hallam, Stanley). Use concise factual summaries as in the notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of editions, authorities, and scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and cite editions, lexica, and scholarly authorities used to support explanations (e.g. Skeat, Richardson, Hallam, Haydn, Murray, Trench, Wright, Camden Society).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give edition details or author and work (occasionally page/section), so readers can verify or consult source; the notes frequently append 'apud Richardson' or cite specific editions and pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthography and variant spellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Record variant historical spellings and recommend the 'proper' or original orthography where relevant (e.g. 'misteries' vs. 'mysteries'; Chaucer's 'Malvesie' variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note folk/false orthographies arising from popular etymologies, show original Latin/Greek/Old English forms, and cite textual instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical clarification through contemporary examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrate lexical senses by quoting contemporary authors and contexts (Chaucer, Shakespeare, Dryden, Bacon, Pepys, Percy Folio, etc.) to show sense and usage in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide short quotations with references and explain how they illuminate the target passage (the notes repeatedly use such parallels to demonstrate senses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual interpretation and emendation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When the printed phrase is awkward or archaic, expound possible grammatical readings, preferred modernizations, or emendations (e.g. explain 'does but resolve' vs. 'resolve' with infinitive; note pleonastic negatives and ambiguous constructions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss alternative parses, indicate which is 'more correct' and why, and give examples of analogous constructions in canonical texts (the notes discuss preferred grammatical forms and ambiguities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain figures of speech and allusions (mythological, allegorical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and explain metaphors, classical/mythological allusions, and symbolic phrases (e.g. 'Hercules pillars' = Straits of Gibraltar; Typhon/Osiris/Isis myths; 'mortalle glasse' = mirror).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize myth or allegory succinctly, cite sources (Pindar, Ovid, Plutarch), and show how the allusion functions in Milton's context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note on sociopolitical/legal terms and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and contextualize legal, ecclesiastical, or institutional terms relevant to the text (e.g. 'canon law', 'conventicle', 'tunnage and poundage', 'Convocation', 'unfrocking').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical/legal definition, note institutional implications (e.g. why duties were contentious), and reference authoritative histories (Hallam, Annals of England).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical nuance and semantic contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out subtle semantic distinctions and contrasts between related words (e.g. 'void' vs 'avoid'; 'step' sense vs modern 'step-' compounds; 'dividual' vs other senses in Paradise Lost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how nuances affect interpretation of the passage and give illustrative citations; the notes repeatedly contrast senses to clarify Milton's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register explanatory notes for readership and rhetorical effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain Milton's rhetorical targets and intended audience labels embedded in diction (e.g. 'professors = Puritans', 'our richest Marchandize, Truth').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify speaker stance, polemical force, and rhetorical strategies; support with historical/political context and contemporary usages cited in the notes.
